Arvory is the regional capital of Agnland. It is situated on mighty cliffs that are facing the sea. Right behind the city is a huge forest which spans hundreds of square kilometres. The bay of Arvory has many fishing companies and the regional trade port. It must be traversed through a steep road that is carved inside the cliffs. Its population is very diverse with a significant Agno-Sordish population coexisting with Rumburgians, Valgs and Sords.

In the 1930's the situation of the city was much worse but due to the efficient mayorship of Lileas Graf the city had a revival period. The living standards rose so many companies started to move in. Land trade with Agnolia increased which created much needed logistical jobs in the area. The construction industry boomed right after. The city still suffers from unemployment and a lack of higher education, but things are much better than before.

There is an old symbolic city hall in the city centre called “Vizeria Agnolia”, which is 150 years old. This reminds people that Arvory was once a part of Greater Agnolia. In the last two decades poverty-stricken extremists started to attack immigrants in a few districts. A huge part of the population condemned these racist acts. Sadly, illegal drug activity is also considered normal in the poorer districts. The new mayor Eric Niel tries to tackle these issues but blames the lack of resources to be able to solve them.

The vibrancy and vitality of Benfi is internationally renowned. Geographically, it is situated by the south-east coast of Sordland. In the early 20s, it contained the only few holiday resorts and nightclubs in the entire country. These were the first Lespian investments that triggered a dramatic shift in the town, that turned from a big fishing town to a large city. It’s income also changed from fishing to tourism and the service sector. Nowadays, international visitors arrive via air and sea to enjoy their summer holidays.

The city serves as a cheaper alternative to many prestigious holiday beaches in the neighbouring countries. Compared to the rest of Sordland, life here is far more adventurous, active and fun. This has drawn many artists to live in this city as Lachaven tends to be a less affordable alternative. Some residents nicknamed the city ‘The Jewel’.

Although it is more active in the spring and summer seasons, during the winter months, the rhythm of the city changes drastically. The usual summer events of surfing, diving and swimming is replaced by prestigious theatre plays, entrepreneurial workshops and artsy cultural festivals during the autumn and winter months. This well organised shift helps the city maintain its spotlight and wealth.

Borin is one of the smallest cities in Sordland. It boasts of having the best wine, cheese and people. The city is surrounded by hills and coastal cliffs that create a wonderful scenery for all to enjoy. The people here are indeed friendly, talkative and social.

The city used to be a town settlement founded by migration period Lespian settlers who in the face of pirate attacks from the sea settled up in the hills for better defense. Historical evidence shows that piracy indeed was less damaging after the relocation. It is around this time where the locals discovered that the climate and ground a little higher up the hills was perfect for vineyards.

Hundreds of years later the tradition of wine making continues here with almost little to no change. Even as industrial machines try to automate agriculture the locals here resort to traditional methods. The elders of Borin don't enjoy the waves of tourists coming and disrupting their lives.

The city is dependant on tourism, wine trade and the attention it gets. Therefore, the strategy of the Municipality remains the same.

Conriat is the third largest city in the Greater Holsord region. It is situated on the Eskel River, which is known for its scenic boat tours from and to the capital. The river creates a vibrant wilderness admired by thousands of weekend visitors.

Conriat is the only port city in the Holsord region, but due to a lack of investment, it can only dock two container ships at any given time. This makes Lachaven the primary destination for international shipping in Central Sordland. Compared to the small civilian port, the humongous Conriat Naval Base, that houses the Sordish Navy, leaves many visitors in nationalistic awe.

In 1789, the city was nearly destroyed in the Great Fire of Conriat because of a Valgslandian Navy attack in which the entire Sordish Fleet was sunk. Six battleships and more than forty support vessels not only decorate the skyline of the coastal city but also employ about fifty thousand residents.

Admiral Schar, who is the commanding officer, is closely related to the mysterious mayor Kris Schar, who also happens to be the one of the shareholders of Underhall Construction. Therefore, the real estate industry favours the area and heavily invests. As a result, many construction jobs employ the citizens.

The hills surrounding Conriat are full of luxury housing bought by the elites of the capital. The city is known for its pure-bred Sarod horses which are used for both national and international racing competitions. They are raised and trained in horse farms owned by privileged country clubs.

Deyr, a city positioned on a fertile river delta, and its neighboring villages, contribute to a substantial portion of Sordland's agricultural yield. The Taurus mountains channel several rivers down to this region, thereby creating extensive farmlands that span across the horizon.

The cityscape of Deyr, which possesses one of the largest metropolitan areas in the nation, comprises three administrative divisions: Old Deyr, New Deyr, and the Outer Farmlands. New Deyr, established in 1911, functions as an Agro-City, conceived as a collective agricultural experiment on an urban scale. The initiative was executed by Heron Walt, the economic advisor to the Kingdom of Sordland, and drew its original inspiration from Valgsland. Featuring an exemplary agricultural infrastructure network, The Grand Bazaar of Deyr stands as a testament to the city's agrarian focus, effectively channeling goods from the farms to businesses or inhabitants.

Located near the city centre, adjacent to the massive Grand Bazaar, is the towering Archsanctuary of Descension, the city's highest structure. This revered Dastnurity shrine attracts pilgrims from all across Sordland, adding to the city's spiritual significance. Not far off, the University of Culture and Nature can be found, further enhancing the city's cultural appeal.

Old Deyr, in stark contrast to its newer counterpart, preserves a sense of timeless charm. Despite the passing centuries, this area continues to shelter an array of settlers with diverse ethnic and religious backgrounds. Landmarks such as the ancient Garden City of Crest and the Temple of Valangir, albeit mostly in ruins, offer glimpses into the past, inspiring its industrious and steadfast inhabitants.

Ethnic diversity defines Deyr, rendering it one of Sordland's most heterogenous cities. New Deyr mostly hosts ethnic Sords, while minority ethnic groups find their home in Old Deyr, where a large Bludish population lives alongside thousands of Wehzeks, Lespians, Derdians and even Old Sords practicing traditional lifestyles. 

Despite its vibrant multiculturalism, the city grapples with undercurrents of ethnic and religious tension, a common challenge for such a diverse region.

Erlory, a city nestled within the Greater Holsord region, is celebrated for its history as the former capital. Despite the grandeur of its past as the vibrant hub of the Markian Empire being somewhat tarnished by repeated sackings, Erlory retains its allure. Many of its historical buildings, bearing the distinct Gothic Revival architecture, have undergone extensive restorations led by Holsord-based construction firms, reviving a sense of the city's former glory.

In addition to its historical charm, Erlory enjoys recognition as the epicenter of Sordish alcohol production. The city's geographic location on a fertile high delta, enriched by the nearby Unger River, cultivates ideal conditions for its famed vineyards and hop farms. Erlory competes with Borin in producing some of Sordland's finest wines, and it houses an abundance of whiskey distilleries. These distilleries have earned international acclaim for their variations of the Erlory Maroon, a whiskey that routinely features in global whiskey championships.

Furthermore, Erlory is host to the expansive Mark Air Force Base and the Air Force Academy, both of which provide employment to a considerable number of local residents. The city's population occasionally finds the frequent buzz of jets an annoyance. Over recent decades, Erlory has attracted the interest of Lespian oligarchs, leading to a rise in upscale real estate and spurring a gentrification debate within the city.

The city of Estord is the most oil rich city of Sordland. It was founded in the 14th century as a silver mining town, but fortunes turned when the mines ran dry. The current situation is bleak; blackouts are routine, public services are barely keeping up and organised crime has taken hold with gang wars bloodying the streets of the city.

The large petroleum industry here employs thousands of workers at less than ideal conditions. Geographically, the city lies between two rivers flowing down from the Sourne mountains in between Sordland and Rumburg. It is beneath the tall Arert mountain which makes for a breath-taking view from the city. There are a few historical sites like the Renan Star Fort east of the city and the monument of despair built during the War of the King.

In its 500-year history multiple wars with Rumburg caused the destruction of the city several times over. Nonetheless Estord flourished again when peace was settled between the Sordland and Rumburg. The real economic boom happened in 1880 when petroleum was discovered.

Sordland’s reliance on foreign oil reduced and Estord was the greatest beneficiary of the black gold rush leading to the formation of Sordish Petroleum. The city grew, and unemployment reached an all time low. A new railway was built to connect the Nargis region to Rumburg. Culturally the constantly shifting social dynamics caused the residents to protect their regional identities. This stands out as a unique case.

The recent worsening of relations with Rumburg, the boom of Lachaven and the 40s economic crisis caused the decline of the city, that lost nearly half of its population to migration to Lachaven and other growing cities with a better future.

Gelsord is the regional capital of the Gelsland region. It is the scientific and technological centre of Sordland. The official motto is ‘Scientia enim est solum iter ante.’ It translates to 'science is the only way forward.'

Located at the city centre is the Gelsord Research Council building. It is led by the rectors of the ten research institutes that are within the metro area. They have a big influence in the administration but are still under the Ministry of Education, Technology & Research led by the minister Ciara Walda. Right next to the G.R.C. is the Forum of Researchers, a cultural building that contains the second largest library in Sordland.

Rumour has it that a secret underground military research facility exists somewhere here. The city also accommodates many new companies that focus on electronics, energy and military technologies. They manufacture telephones, radios, cameras and many other technologies which are sold all over the country and even exported abroad.

Therefore, even though the population living in the city is not large the GDP per capita is very high. This attracts accomplished students who are adept in the technology field. That’s why if the smartest aren’t going to Gelsord they are likely to be going abroad either to United Contana or Arcasia.

Holsord is the vibrant capital city of Sordland, known for its significant political, cultural, and educational institutions. The city's central hub is Capitol Park, a large recreational area surrounded by numerous key landmarks. Among these is the Presidential Palace, a towering architectural structure that stands out prominently in the cityscape, and the Grand National Assembly, a pivotal venue where representatives convene to discuss and enact legislation.

The city center is notable for its concentration of governmental institutions such as the Supreme Court and the Ministry of Justice. The presence of these institutions lends Holsord a distinct political atmosphere, with individuals involved in bureaucracy, politics, military, and academics frequently seen in the city's streets.

Holsord is also known for its thriving educational landscape, particularly on the eastern side of the city. Here, one finds the Holsord State University, Kingshill University, and the Imperial Markian University, collectively known as 'The League of the Trident'. These universities are among the country's most prestigious educational institutions.

However, the city's administrative presence is balanced by a significant military presence. The Ministry of Defense and the expansive 'Camp Strongarm' are also located here, housing the largest military contingent within a city in the country. The camp is home to the elite 101st, 102nd, and 103rd Presidential Guard Divisions, which form part of the 1st Army. This marks a shift from the city's past, when military forces were decentralized and not permitted within the capital.

People from all over Sordland are drawn to Holsord in pursuit of better opportunities, contributing to the city's dynamic social fabric. The city is a microcosm of the country, presenting a juxtaposition of understanding and ignorance, wealth and poverty, power and weakness, reflecting the diverse realities of its inhabitants.

Jen, located in the Greater Holsord Region of Sordland, is a city distinguished by its strongly nationalist population. Situated among a series of hills, the city borders the nation of Lespia to the south.

The local economy is driven predominantly by the transportation and storage sectors, as a considerable share of goods from Lespia, particularly from Merlotia, pass through Jen. Upon arrival, these goods are stored, catalogued, and then transported onwards to Holsord. The city's surroundings present a barren landscape, ill-suited for agriculture. A nearby river offers some life to the surrounding areas, but its swift current makes it impractical for other uses.

Politically, the citizens of Jen were initially steadfast in their support for the United Sordland Party and its former leader, Tarquin Soll. However, changes in leadership precipitated a shift in political loyalty towards the Nationalist Front Party, making Jen a prominent stronghold for this party. The city has subsequently earned a reputation as a haven for those with more extreme views, who struggle to find acceptance in other parts of the country.

Lachaven is a sprawling port city and the primary trade hub of Sordland. Tall mountains surround it, creating a near to perfect natural harbour, which bewilders new visitors. Most of the international sea trade to Sordland flows through this city. Many Lachaveners and Eastern Merkopans call the city ‘The Gateway’ for that particular reason besides others.

Dozens of container and cruise ships can be observed anchoring and leaving port within the same hour. The top five exports of the city are furniture, motor vehicles, clothing, electrical machinery and pharmaceuticals. They are exported in mass to countries like Arcasia, Lespia, Valgsland and United Contana, providing significant economic wealth to the area. The National Business Council has a board full of wealthy individuals who spend their good fortunes on their luxurious lifestyle.

The Lespian architecture of Lachaven creates a very unique skyline compared to the other less imaginative cities. This city is also home to numerous theatres, art exhibitions and a glamorously vivid night life known throughout the land. The famous Republic Avenue stretches for several kilometres through the city. It is decorated with palm trees and sculptures from many notable artists. The Evaria Gallery of Art, The Maroon Theatre and the Lachaven Opera House draws thousands of art lovers every month.

The two most significant educational institutions here are the Lachaven Business School and the Isambard University of Lachaven. In addition, the lover’s street filled with the best bars and clubs cause many young students to flock to the city to enjoy an intriguing weekend. Moreover, a booming tourism industry exists with nearly a million tourists a month coming to see historical landmarks such as the Basilisk of Baal or the Great Library of Wruhec.

Most of the People’s Freedom and Justice Party support comes from this city even though the party was founded in Holsord. As can be expected, the most liberal part of the population in Sordland resides here. Obviously, it is not very hard to spot them with their privileged, defensive and somewhat educated behaviour.

Situated on the hilly and shrub filled Gruni countryside is Leiren. One finds solitude here is unlike any other place. It’s not about the geography but about the philosophy. Upon entrance one notices that life flows much slower. People aren’t stressed, nor much concerned about what is happening in the country or in the world.

The city is famous for the variety of healing herbs it grows thanks to the unique climate conditions. These vital ingredients are sold to pharmacies in the region and beyond.

The idea of the slow city came from the successful mayor Delmond Locke. His municipal administration set a new standard on how to properly utilize city funds to the benefit of the people. Instead of wasting funds on luxurious cars, bodyguards and estates, he spent them on aiding the poor, building more recreational areas and reducing the price of local public transport.

Within one-decade the amount of people coming to the city tripled the ones leaving. Leiren became the quiet alternative to Benfi.

Lenkurg is the second largest city in the Agnland region. Economically it benefits from the strategic position between Lachaven and Arvory. Many logistics companies have depots to support the trade towards Agnolia. The small Lenkurg port has minimal but still crucial ship activity.

During the last decade the decaying infrastructure has hampered economic growth, but a thriving fishing industry has kept many Lenkurgians employed. The thousands of tons of salmon are packaged and distributed all around the country. Many Sordish citizens enjoy it with salt and butter. Though relatively cold compared to Benfi, the best beach of Agnland is located here. Being close to the sea gives a sense of commonality because everybody swims together during summer months.

The old city centre has landmarks from the Markian era. Lenkurg is less diverse compared to Arvory but it has a large portion of Wruhecist believers that have formed a sub-culture. The recent influx of migrants coming from Agnolia caused somewhat of a housing crisis which the construction companies from Arvory are exploiting.

Morna is the regional capital of the Lorren region. It is the largest and most industrialized city in Lorren. Founded by industrialists of the Renan Aristocracy, it was later taken over by a nationalization plan of King Egmund. Morna began to supply many cities with the huge forestry industry it developed. The timber here was even sold abroad in countries like Valgsland or Lespia.

Today, Morna shows clear advantages and disadvantages of the industrialization period. While the big companies offer relatively good wages, they also cause a lot of pollution and damage to nature in the area. This has drawn the attention of the Nature Preservation Foundation, which frequently organizes strikes and protests against the biggest corporations who neglect the environment.

The Nedam Mining Group, Wudlan Forestry and Sordish Grid Corporations employ a large portion of the populace in the city. The city and these huge corporations suffer from a logistical issue. Nearly forty percent of all goods from Morna are exported overseas, but there is no nearby port to ship the goods away. This forces goods to travel to Holsord, and then to Conriat creating logistical delays and costs.

The forest and the wildlife surrounding the city is praised by many. The fact that the city is large and pollutant forces people who want to enjoy nature to go to Morbel or Vesord. Research also suggests that artifacts from the migration period are underneath certain parts of the city. These are revealed during new construction projects and cause delays due to excavations taking place. There are two reasons people go to Morna. It's either to get a job or to make one.

Narbel is the smallest and poorest city in the Nargis region. It is located at the skirts of the Cavendir Mountain. Centuries past this town used to be positioned on a very important trade route that went towards the old capital of the Markian Empire.

Narbel used to heavily benefit from this trade, and got quite enriched from it. In the past hundred years the city experienced a massive economic downturn. As most of the attention of the governments in Sordland went more inland, many old rural trade hubs like Narbel were forgotten. The previous governments weren't interested to invest in cities with a lack of natural resources. A recent discovery of natural gas resources in Narbel drastically changed the situation.

A large investment from the Gasom Corporation boosted economic growth. The city still harbours a large population of poverty-stricken residents, who increasingly had to rely on farming and hunting for self-sufficiency. The situation also led to starvation, which became a big problem in the 1920's, but was quickly solved when the state intervened and subsidized bread and rice to Narbel.

Ribery barely gained the city status in 1950. Mainly due to the taxes it could pay in comparison to other smaller towns. If the city has anybody to thank it is the tourists who often visit the famous historical Caves of Antera site underneath the city itself.

It provides the locals great economic opportunity. Many rent out their houses or event sell property to make a lot of money. The city is also very special due to the fact that it can see the gulf clearly from it, and is the only city that can provide that except for Lachaven. Many don't like to swim in the cold waters but very much enjoy the scenic hillside houses for relaxation. Some locals have been more vocal about the shift in the tradition and life in Ribery, but that doesn't change the fact that, without tourism this city would be very much lost.

The real estate industry also began to invest heavily in the outskirts of the urban area in the hopes of cashing out of the tourist influx. Ribery is beautiful and worth a visit. The locals say that, if you have been to Ribery once, then you have been to Ribery a million times.

One of the most famous Riberians was Giralt of Ribery, the famous winemaker of Erlory.

Sarna, a city situated within the region of Bergia, shares its borders with the nation of Lespia. It is a diverse city, home to a small, culturally rich enclave of Wehzeks and Lespians.

The city also serves as a gateway to the natural wonders of the southernmost reaches of the Maris Forest, which extends north-eastward all the way to Gelsord. Local folklore tells of a forest giant that has dwelled here since the first century, though city dwellers often dismiss this as mere myth.

The city centre of Sarna presents a labyrinthine network of streets. This organic, rather than planned, layout lends the city a unique charm when viewed from above. However, the complexity of the street network can result in significant traffic congestion, particularly during rush hour. As a solution, the mayor has promoted cycling as a preferred mode of transportation.

An important historical shift occurred five decades ago when Heron Walt initiated an experiment rendering Sarna and the city of Merlotia completely tax-exempt. Contrary to initial expectations, the creation of this free-trade zone proved highly successful, catalysing sustained economic prosperity for Sarna.

The city of Uziren is one of the few majority Bludish cities in Sordland. It is located at a very strategic area bordering Rumburg, Wehlen and Lespia. The city also has a large population of Wehzeks living at the west side. The notorious Gumren Military Outpost is located next to the border and currently assists the high security border crossing.

Economically, Uziren is reliant on the agricultural industry. Many Bludish citizens are very experienced herders who sell high quality products to the market at Uziren, which is transported towards the major trade hubs. The city also has several cheap motels that provide hospitality services to pilgrims who are travelling to Deyr from neighbouring countries.

The locals here call the region Bludia instead of Bergia. Several nationalistic Bludish groups reportedly declared their support for the Bludish Freedom Front. This upsets many Sords and has also triggered the government to assign a 24-hour special riot force that was activated in the 1930's.

Valgen is regarded as one of the most important cities of the east. Its rich multi-cultural history is admired among historians and sociologists. Moreover, it is the main logistical artery that links the liberal region of Gruni to Lespia. The river delta and the warm climate result in very fertile ground for fruit agriculture.

Therefore, Valgen is known to be the primary citrus producer in the country, surpassing even Deyr. The city also has the second largest hydroelectric power plant in the country. It was built with the help of Lespian engineers three decades ago.

Once upon a time, the city was nicknamed 'the Lachaven of the East', but that torch has slowly been passed on to Benfi. The emigration triggered by the economic crisis caused a huge change in urban society. The city became poorer and living standards worsened, so many moved away to find better prospects. This caused the Lespian investments being retracted out of the city, which caused further unemployment the city couldn’t recover from.

During the thousand-year existence as a city, Valgen was controlled by several different countries and people. The tribe of Valgs were the founders of the city. Later it switched hands between the Markians, Lespians and the Sords. Most of the ethnic Valgs still living in the city left and settled to their recently founded homeland, Valgos, while the thousands of Lespians who lived under the Markian Empire also decided to settle in their newly independent country.

Nowadays only few of the old Valg and Lespian traditions are being practiced by Sordish citizens. However, some ideas, like freedom and equality that formed through living together have continued throughout generations.

The Federation of Anrakan Isles, commonly known as Anraka, is a federal republic comprising a strategically located archipelago between the continents of Merkopa and Contana. Its vibrant capital, Pada Dolhi, serves as the political and economic hub of the nation. President Aditya Shikra, a descendant of the legendary pirate queen Ishani Shikra, leads the federation. Ishani is celebrated for her decisive role in the Battle of the Sirens, where Anrakan forces successfully resisted Kontanian and Arcasian colonial powers.

Anraka’s maritime history is rooted in resistance against colonial forces during the age of Arcasian and Kontanian expansion. The islanders, renowned for their naval expertise and piracy, united in 1944 under external pressures and the need for a cohesive defense. This union formed the modern federation, blending pirate codes, merchant republic traditions, and emerging democratic principles. Governance today reflects this legacy, combining strict law enforcement with participatory decision-making, though income disparities remain entrenched due to a rigid caste system.

Anraka’s economic strength lies in its dominance of naval technology, offshore energy extraction, and maritime exploration. However, this progress has come at a steep environmental cost. Extensive oil drilling, deep-sea mining, and heavy industrialization have led to significant ocean pollution, destruction of coral reefs, and declining marine biodiversity. While its advanced naval vessels and aircraft carriers are world-renowned, their production and operation contribute to the nation’s high carbon emissions. Anraka has faced growing international criticism for its environmental practices, but economic priorities and global trade ambitions continue to drive its industrial output.

Despite these challenges, Anraka remains a powerful maritime nation. Its institutions, shaped by the adventurous spirit of its pirate heritage, foster innovation and resilience. Maritime education, particularly in naval engineering, produces skilled seafarers who uphold the nation’s dominance on the seas. While environmental conservation efforts are limited, Anraka prioritizes maintaining its economic influence and naval superiority, often at the expense of its natural environment.

The Republic of Arcasia, commonly referred to as Arcasia, is a constitutional republic located in Western Merkopa and recognized as one of the world's foremost superpowers. Its capital, Ventrie City, serves as the nation’s political hub and the financial capital of the global capitalist system. The current president, Dwight Walker, is a renowned figure known for his Rumburgian heritage and for overseeing one of the most ambitious economic reform programs in modern history. 

The modern Arcasian state was established in 1823 following the overthrow of King Jonathan XII and the collapse of the Kingdom of Arcas, which in its later years had been effectively dominated by a clique of wealthy Rumburgian merchant families. The revolution was led by the “Éclaireurs de la Liberté” under the leadership of Louis Beaumont, setting off a cascade of revolts across the globe known as the Century of Revolutions. By the late 19th century, Arcasia had emerged as a global power, anchoring its influence in the spread of capitalism, liberal democracy, and military dominance. 

Arcasia secured the world’s largest economy by nominal GDP in the early 20th century. Its corporate sector expanded across continents, universities grew into elite academic institutions, and political freedoms remained broadly protected. At the same time, structural inequalities persisted, particularly between urban financial centers and underdeveloped regions, and its global conduct has come under scrutiny for reported abuses abroad. 

Since 1947, Arcasia has been led by President Dwight Walker and the New Democratic Concord. Under Walker’s administration, the implementation of the Walker Plan has transformed the national economy. Key industries such as telecommunications, education, transportation, healthcare, and military contracting underwent sweeping deregulation and privatization. Private defense firms like Cerberus International and Palantor Security Solutions rose to prominence during this era. The resulting economic boom gave rise to the cultural vision known as the “Arcasian Dream,” celebrating meritocracy, entrepreneurial success, and upward mobility. 

Arcasia is a founding member of the Arcasian Treaty Organization, officially established in 1945 under President Renald Revoutier. The alliance was created in response to the Contanan Security Pact and was later expanded under Walker’s leadership. ATO unifies member states in a common military and economic framework, promoting open markets and regional defense. Its strategic posture now includes missile defense cooperation and nuclear deterrence planning. 

The nation is also a founding member of the Organization for Merkopan Economic Cooperation and holds significant sway in the Alliance of Nations. The nation encompasses much of the western Merkopan coast, parts of the northwest interior, and includes large undeveloped areas such as the Western Merkopan Desert. Its political system, corporate networks, and military alliances continue to shape the structure of global power well into the second half of the century.

Kyrute, officially recognized as the Republic of Kyrute, is an island nation located in the heart of the Antacean Sea. It consists of three main landmasses - Kyrutium, Anatium, and Adrium, along with numerous smaller islands. Kyrute is governed as a parliamentary republic with elements of direct democracy. Its capital city is Konstantium, with the current leader being Chancellor Inos Adriumer.

Historically, Kyrute is believed to have been the epicenter of the legendary Antacean civilization. However, concrete evidence regarding this civilization's existence remains elusive. Recent scientific findings suggest the presence of advanced mega-cities on Kyrutium as early as the 5th millennium BH. In pursuit of further evidence of submerged cities, scientists and explorers are currently engaged in extensive undersea explorations.

From the 3rd to the 9th century, the islands were fragmented into eight smaller kingdoms that were perpetually at war. These kingdoms were later unified by Konstanta the Great into an elective monarchy with Konstantium as its base.

Starting from the 11th century, Kyrute transformed into a critical trade hub within the Antacean Sea. This strategic importance attracted the attention of neighboring empires, leading to numerous attempted invasions. Kyrute boasts a history of impressive defensive victories, successfully resisting powerful forces such as the North Xinans, Rezenids, and Markians. Despite numerous successful defenses against the Valgos Empire, Kyrute eventually became a Valgish territory in the 17th century. Valgish Kyrutium evolved into a significant economic powerhouse and served as the naval and trade operations center for the empire until 1853. Inspired by revolutions in Merkopa, Kyrutean Nationalists revolted and established the independent Republic of Kyrute after a series of brutal wars against the empire.

Since its inception, the republic has maintained a policy of diplomatic neutrality. The seizure of Valgish imperial assets on the island and a series of successful economic policies led to an economic boom on the island. Kyrute has not participated in a war since 1853 and pursues an active foreign policy, including spearheading peace-building processes worldwide. It is a founding member of the Alliance of Nations and hosts the organization's headquarters on international territory in Konstantium.

Kyrute ranks as one of the world's most developed countries, boasting the highest nominal wealth per adult. It is known for its strong record on civil rights, political life, and quality of life. The nation has gained international renown as a destination for exiles and political refugees and serves as a center of offshore banking.

Kyrute is a member of the Antacean Free Trade Association (AFTA), the Organization for Merkopan Economic Development (OMEC), and is a founding member of the Alliance of Nations.

The Republic of Lespia is a parliamentary republic located in Eastern Merkopa, with its capital in Perla, a historic center of commerce, finance, and cultural life. The nation occupies a strategic coastline along the Antecaen Sea and maintains several outlying territories. It is currently governed by the center-right Democrazia Lespia party, under the leadership of Prime Minister Patricio Alvarez. 

Lespia’s origins trace back to the early 9th century as a sovereign kingdom. Conquered by the Markian Empire in the 11th century, it remained under imperial rule for nearly six hundred years. Upon regaining independence in the 17th century, Lespia restructured into a federation of duchies and city-states, governed through an elective monarchy based in Perla. 

During the Century of Revolutions, Lespia peacefully transitioned to a republican form of government in 1850, inspired by revolutionary events in Arcasia. In the decades that followed, it expanded its maritime presence and established colonial footholds in Rika, bolstering its status as a naval and trade power in the region. 

Modern Lespia emerged as an economic powerhouse during the 1930s and 1940s, as rapid industrial growth and financial modernization transformed the country into one of Eastern Merkopa’s leading economies. This period of expansion culminated in the 1948 general election, in which Patricio Alvarez led Democrazia Lespia to victory over Prime Minister Cauren Fidalco and the ruling Partito Libertà Nazionale. 

After taking office in 1949, Alvarez introduced a new economic vision known as Lespian Protectionism, built on theories he co-developed with his mentor, Serdin Alvarro. His administration established the Lespian Capital Protection Agency and forged partnerships with the Magical Eight, a coalition of major domestic corporations. These efforts aimed to insulate the national economy from foreign volatility, strengthen local industry, and secure capital independence. 

In 1950, Lespia formally joined the Arcasian Treaty Organization, marking a pivotal shift in its geopolitical orientation. The decision reinforced Lespia’s alignment with Arcasia and integrated the country into the broader capitalist defense and economic framework of the West. As Cold War tensions rose with United Contana and the Contanan Security Pact, Lespia’s strategic location and economic strength positioned it as a key regional ally in the containment effort. Although praised for its economic revival, Alvarez’s leadership has sparked internal debate over increasing inequality, corporate influence, and the growing divide between urban affluence and rural poverty. While political freedoms remain strong, concerns persist regarding the erosion of civil rights and the consolidation of economic power. 

Today, Lespia flourishes as a hub of tourism, cultural innovation, and regional diplomacy. It is a member of the Arcasian Treaty Organization, the Organization for Merkopan Economic Development, and holds a permanent seat in the Alliance of Nations, reflecting its global influence and strong integration within the international community.

Pales, officially known as the Grand Duchy of Pales, is a coastal country located in southeastern Merkopa. The only country it borders is the Kingdom of Rizia. The country's capital is the Port of Pales, and it is governed by a monarch, Duke Axel Reinhart.

The culture, people, and languages of Pales are deeply intertwined with its Rizian neighbors. Though the official national language is Palean (closely related to Rizian, and sometimes considered a Rizian dialect or a language invented by Valgish colonizers), Rizian and Valgish are also used in administrative and judicial proceedings.

Pales first emerged in the 10th century when Count Rezna acquired a rocky coastal region in southern Rizia and built the first Rezenid-era fortifications, known as Paleaccis, in the modern-day city of Pales and its surrounding area. Over the centuries, Pales thrived under the Rezenid and Markian empires and later became part of the Kingdom of Rizia when it seceded from the Markian Empire in the 17th century.

During the 17th century, the port city of Pales became one of Eastern Merkopa's most important trade hubs and served as the main port for the Kingdom of Rizia. However, in the late 17th century, the Valgos Empire occupied the city, forcing the Rizian government to cede administrative control of the port. Despite losing its most crucial port, the region of Greater Pales remained part of Rizia until the 19th century.

As promised by Duke Willem of Monqiz during the War of Rizian Succession, Valgos took control over the Pales region and the coastal areas of Morella along the Gulf of Nal in 1810, integrating it into the empire. The Duchy of Pales was established soon after, unifying Greater Pales and the coastal regions of Morella under a Valgish duke.

After the 1920 revolution in the Valgos Empire, the region went through a time of political upheaval before proclaiming itself an independent country, the Grand Duchy of Pales. In the meantime, the Republic of Morella took advantage of the instability to reclaim its coastline and former capital city, Cavette. Later, the Kingdom of Rizia swiftly retook the northern parts of Greater Pales in military operations with minimal casualties. However, with financial and military aid from Lespia, the Reinhart family maintained control and successfully defended the southeastern cities in the duchy. 

In the 1930s, the country saw rapid economic growth and militarized its borders with the help of the Republic of Lespia. Both countries signed numerous cooperation agreements, resulting in the Grand Duchy's increasing reliance on Lespia.

In 1947, Duke Njolma's brief ban on the Rizian language led to heightened tensions between pro-Rizian and pro-Palesian factions. This controversial move compelled Njolma to abdicate, paving the way for his brother, Axel, to assume the throne. Axel, widely admired by the Rizian-speaking community, was officially crowned as Axel Reinhart in 1948, a year following his brother's resignation. 

The Grand Duchy of Pales is a developed country with a robust economy, boasting one of the world's highest GDPs per capita. The city of Pales was declared an ESCAN Heritage Site in 1950 due to the remarkable preservation of the Rezenid-era fortifications. The country has an above-average record on civil rights but below-average political freedoms.

Pales is a member of the Organization for Merkopan Economic Development (OMEC).

The Republic of Qinal, commonly known as Qinal, is a strategically situated country, predominantly on the Xenal Peninsula in Northern Xina with a minor segment extending into Southeast Merkopa. To the north, Qinal shares borders with Morella and the Free Cities, while it is flanked by the Sea of Nem to the west, Neqis to the south, and the Antacean Sea to the east. 

Qinal is unique for being the only Xinan member of the Arcasian Treaty Organization (ATO). The nation's political framework is a parliamentary republic, with the current Prime Minister, Reza Ngoda, in office. Its capital, Moustapal, is the nation's most populous city. Ancient civilizations such as the Xenali, Gertic, and the North Xinan Empire once thrived in the area known today as Qinal. The 8th century saw the first wave of Qinali migration. Initially arriving as raiders and mercenaries at the service of the North Xinan Empire, they eventually established themselves as the ruling class of the Xenal region.

Qinal's religious landscape was profoundly reshaped in the 11th century when the Mousser invaders propagated Zaranism, a religion that is still predominant today. The Markians, during the Great Invasion of Merkopa, managed to seize most of the peninsula's northern territories. However, their advance was brought to a halt at Moustapal in 1582 by the Mousser Empire, thereby concluding the 29-Year-War.

During the period between the 17th and 19th centuries, the Valgos Empire asserted its dominance over Qinal's eastern coasts and northern territories. However, a bloody conflict in 1821 resulted in the Qinali regaining control over these regions. The dissolution of the Mousser Empire in 1905 paved the way for the Qinali Independence Movement, which subsequently led to the establishment of the Republic of Qinal.

Under the leadership of the first president, a series of reforms transformed Qinal into a unitary parliamentary republic and a significant military power. In 1947, the country became a member of the ATO. As a regional powerhouse situated at a geopolitically crucial location, Qinal has faced allegations of multiple sabotage incidents by Morella and the Free Cities. Boasting a large economy, Qinal is known for its above-average civil rights and commendable political freedoms. Zaranism is the predominant religion among the majority of its population.

Qinal's international affiliations include being a founding member of the Xinan Economic Cooperation (XEC) and a member of the Alliance of Nations.

The Kingdom of Rizia, colloquially known as Rizia, is a semi-constitutional monarchy led by King Romus Toras. It is positioned on the eastern coast of South Merkopa's peninsula. The Kingdom is neighbored by Wehlen, Morella, and the Grand Duchy of Pales, and separated from Lespia by the Sudis Sea.

Rizia's name finds its roots in the Rezenid Empire, a powerful ancient confederation that dominated much of Southern Merkopa at the beginning of the first millennium. The ruling Reznas family strategically established their stronghold, Drazon (later renamed Porte Drazon), at the Zpana River's mouth, taking advantage of the fertile soil.

The region fell to the Markian Empire in the early 1100s, which built roads, bridges, and aqueducts, and mined small amounts of gold to support their expansion. This rule lasted until the 1600s, when the Rubaz family led an independence movement, forming the Kingdom of Rizia comprising three semi-autonomous provinces – Brenas, Valenqiris, and Montaklar – governed from the central domain of Rizia Imperii. In the 1800s, a split in the Rubaz family led to the War of Rizan Succession, causing a five-year bloody conflict that involved several external powers. After the war, the Toras family took the crown, with the Sazon and Azaro families controlling Brenas and Montaklar.

Rizia's Golden Age occurred in the late 1800s under Queen Lyza "The Great" Toras, driven by advancements in gold mining technology. However, this era ended with the reign of Lyza's son, Valero "The Frail," whose unsuccessful attempts to retake Pales led to rebellion. Despite initial struggles, the Crown regained some of its economic stability thanks to alliances and the discovery of natural gas fields. Today, it boasts one of the highest GDPs on the continent due to the wealth of its nobility. Some citizens do enjoy a high quality of life due to good salaries and competitively well-funded social services.

The government holds part-ownership of large corporations, with Rizian Royal Gold being the most significant. Despite commendations for its free healthcare, low tax rates, and progressive women's rights policies, the human rights record of the country has been criticized for the unequal treatment of citizens and non-citizens and harsh punishments for protesters. More recently, diminishing natural resources have caused strain on the treasury of the Golden Kingdom, which in the last decades has bid farewell to its Golden Age and entered a more challenging period.

Rizia is a member of the Organization for Merkopan Economic Development (OMEC), the Guild of Royal Allies for Commercial Exchange (GRACE), and the Alliance of Nations.

Kingdom of Rumburg, commonly known as Rumburg, is a constitutional monarchy situated in northern Merkopa. The country's capital is Thornbourgh and its monarch is Queen Beatrice Livingston. It is the largest country on the Merkopan continent by size, spanning the entire north from west to east, and is a founding member of The Guild of Royal Allies for Commercial Exchange (GRACE), which it has traditionally led in policy and coordination.

Rumburg initially emerged as a march of the Rums around the 7th century and later, with the Migration, developed into the heartland for the Kingdom of the Rums. In 1599, Rumburg broke away from the Markian Empire and established its own kingdom. In the early 19th century, Rumburg transitioned into a constitutional monarchy as King Uthred Livingston transferred powers to the Council of State and later to the Parliament of Rumburg. The royal line is commonly listed as Alfred I Livingston, Uthred Livingston, Elswyn Livingston, Alfred II Livingston, and Beatrice Livingston, with succession governed by the Succession Ordinance and regencies by the Regency Act, which places full authority in a regent until the monarch reaches the age of 18.

In the nineteenth century Rumburg rose as a major power in Merkopa after colonizing and industrializing vast northern territories of steppe, tundra, and ice. During this period the crown gradually absorbed hereditary duchies into centralized crown lands, with industrial expansion driven by collectivized production programs and penal labor. The result was rapid growth in mining, rail infrastructure, and military manufacturing, which positioned Rumburg among the continent's leading military-industrial powers. Rumburg historically maintained close commercial relations with the Kingdom of Arcas; following the Arcasian Revolution of 1823, this relationship evolved into a complex rivalry between the continent's foremost monarchical and republican powers.

Rumburg was shaped by repeated interstate conflicts, including the Central Merkopa War (1837–1866), which ended in the Treaty of Alfretsrat, and the Treaty of Crimsrad (1846), which expanded access to Agnolian ports. After suffering extensively during the Fifteen Day War against Sordland, the country developed the KA-74 automatic rifle, which became one of the most widely used weapons on the continent. Later, the False Crowns War culminated in the Treaty of Glenhill and secured strategic rail and border regimes. Rumburg's economy also came to be shaped by large private-state industrial actors, including Rumburg Emerald Energy.

In November 1921, Beatrice Livingston acceded to the throne at sixteen following the death of King Alfred II, ruling under a regency headed by Duke Eadric Wulfsbury until she reached majority. Her early reign was marked by the War of Broken Wills (1921–1924) and the subsequent Treaty of Konstantium, followed by the War of the Ridges. It also included the sending of aid to Rizia during the 1926 uprising and the formal abandonment of a proposed Eastern Merkopan Pact with the Valgos Empire following its revolution in favor of closer ties with Arcasia. In her later reign, her foreign policy was codified under the title "The Great Unification.” Despite official denials, Rumburg is believed to have been heavily involved in both the Wehlen Civil War and the Sordish Civil War.

Rumburg's internal politics are described through three major parliamentary factions: the Greater Rummish Union Party, the Crown Preservation Party, and the Constitutional Reform Party, which compete over foreign policy, industrial strategy, and the balance between court influence and parliamentary governance.

The nation has a strong economy and a below average civil rights record with limited political freedoms, and it remains heavily oriented toward strategic industry and military technology. Through extensive state promotion of science and defense research, it has experienced rapid technological development and is believed to maintain significant experimental weapons programs. Despite having extensive northern natural resources, Rumburg imports large volumes of raw materials to sustain its growing industrial base.

It is a member of OMEC, GRACE, and the Alliance of Nations.

Agnolia, officially the Republic of Agnolia, is a parliamentary republic located in Eastern Merkopa. Its capital, Staalport, serves as the country's principal maritime, administrative, and customs center. The republic is currently governed by the centrist Nurist Democratic Union Party under Prime Minister Maartin Van Hoorten.

The name Agnolia derives from the Agno tribes who settled the region in the early seventh century. For centuries the Agno peoples lived under the dominance of the Markian tribes and later the Markian Empire. Statehood emerged in 1600 with the creation of the Kingdom of Agnolia. The monarchy lasted seventy-five years before Queen Lenna married Erik Renan of Sordland, forming the Agnolian-Sordish Commonwealth. This dynastic union endured until 1739 and was followed by the proclamation of the Republic of Agnolia in 1740. The early republic functioned as a merchant polity led by a Grand Stadehalder and the Grand Assembly, and during the Century of Revolutions evolved into a parliamentary system with an elected prime minister.

In the nineteenth century, the Land Conversion Acts dismantled aristocratic tenure and placed large estates under the Republican Sovereign Wealth Trust, transforming the country's institutional foundations. Staalport developed into one of the most important trading hubs in Eastern Merkopa. Throughout this period Agnolia relied on its relationship with Sordland as an informal counterweight to pressure from Rumburg and the Valgos Empire, while cooperation with Rumburg was viewed as a pragmatic counterweight to the growing power of the Valgos Empire.

A period of economic expansion in the late 1910s enabled naval modernization. In 1920, amid the collapse of the Valgos Empire, Agnolia occupied and fortified Heljiland. The following year it reclaimed Port Grim. Tensions with Rumburg escalated after the Agnolian High Court invalidated foreign inheritance claims over the Dome estates in May 1921, triggering the War of Broken Wills. The conflict concluded with the Treaty of Konstantium. Despite territorial losses, Agnolia preserved its sovereignty, parliamentary institutions, and control over the Staalport trade corridor. 

The economy receded in the late 1930s and the republic endured a major crisis in 1940, accepting financial aid from both United Contana and Arcasia. During the late 1940s, more than a million Agnolians emigrated to Sordland amid poverty and food insecurity.

The Otkende administration has prioritized infrastructure development, overseeing the construction of railways, tunnels, highways, and the expansion of shipyards and manufacturing sectors. However, the government faces criticism over its handling of ongoing conflicts on Helji Island between local Valgish and Agnolian populations, and its diplomatic posture toward Rumburg and the strategic city of Dome is widely perceived as passive. Unfavorable trade agreements with countries including Sordland, Lespia, Rizia, and Valgsland have contributed to a significant trade deficit, fueling public dissatisfaction.

The country's political landscape is organized around the Social Democratic Party, the Nurist Democratic Union, the nationalist-leaning National Vigilance Party, and the Civic Traditionalist Party, which maintains monarchist sympathies despite operating within the republican system. Limited Malenyevist and Valgslandian socialist sympathies are present among industrial and port communities.

The country is known for its steel, coal, and fishing industries, and has an average civil rights record with strong political freedoms. Agnolia is a member of OMEC and the Alliance of Nations and continues to advocate arbitration, maritime commerce, and multilateral diplomacy in regional affairs.

United Contana is a federalist socialist republic situated on the continent of Contana, and considered as a superpower of the world. It is a union of multiple socialist republics spanning Contana. The country is a one-party state, governed by the Communist Party with Kyow as its capital. It is led by Chairman Leon "Malenyev" Chavatangakwunua.

United Contana had its roots in the 1907 Revolution, when the revolutionaries of the Rotski, led by Malenyev, overthrew the Kontanian government which had replaced the autocratic regime of the king during the Century of Revolutions. In 1910, after a civil war ending in the Rotskis' victory, the United Contana was formed by a treaty that united the Kontanian, Transcontanan, Kyovian, and Byelocontanan republics of the Contana continent.

Malenyev replaced the market economy with a command economy which led to a period of rapid industrialization and collectivization in the United Contana. During this period, rapid economic development resulted in dramatic improvements in the average standard of living, particularly in urban areas. The country saw major reforms under the ideology of Malenyevism. It promoted the idea of the permanent revolution abroad and supported social revolutions in nearby states with early-stage capitalism. United Contana grew its influence around the world with Malenyevist ideas and rose to become a superpower of the world.

United Contana is currently locked in a fierce global ideological battle with Arcasia. Both powers are in a race of influence around the globe. United Contana has been growing its influence around the world by supporting less fortunate nations with their problems, supporting revolutionaries and unions abroad. They have already influenced several revolutions to occur which led to the founding of new Marco-Malenyevist nations.

The nation has a very strong economy and an average civil rights record with few political freedoms. Thanks to the education reforms and heavy promotion of sciences, they experienced a technological golden age and currently are considered to be ahead of their rivals in the world. The continent is very resource rich and United Contana uses this as a means to spread their influence around the globe. It tends to export natural resources more than any nation in the world, and in exchange, sets up military bases in strategic countries.

It is the founding member of the Contanan Security Pact (CSP) which was created against the growing threat of Arcasian Capitalism and neo-imperialism. It is also a permanent member of the Alliance of Nations.

The Democratic Republic of Valgsland, commonly referred to as Valgsland, is a socialist republic located on the island of Valgos and its surrounding archipelago. Governed by the People’s Party, the nation is headquartered in the capital city of Haelm. Its current head of government is Chancellor Emmerich Hegel, under whose leadership the country has undergone wide-reaching reforms. 

Valgsland traces its cultural roots to the Valg tribes, who settled the island in the 11th century. Before their arrival, the region was home to the Galmanic peoples, and over time, Valgsland developed a unique insular culture, distinct from its continental neighbors in Mark and Sord. By the 16th century, Valgsland emerged as a formidable naval and colonial power. Known then as the Empire of Valgos, it held one of the largest navies in the world and maintained a vast colonial presence across Rika and Xina until the 19th century. 

Following decades of decline, the monarchy was overthrown in the Valgslandian Revolution of 1920, led by Wilhelm Ulbrik, who established a socialist state inspired by Malenyevism in United Contana. The early republic adopted a command economy, granted independence to Valgos’ former colonies, and pursued internal consolidation through extensive purges and centralized rule. 

Emmerich Hegel, a key figure in the revolution and long-time member of the ruling party, gradually rose through the political ranks. Though publicly aligned with Ulbrik, Hegel began advocating for an alternative socialist model known as Valgslandian Socialism, which emphasized decentralization, participatory governance, and regional economic autonomy. After Ulbrik’s death in 1940, Hegel was elected Chancellor and initiated a major political shift by distancing Valgsland from strict Malenyevist doctrine and reducing state repression through democratic reforms. 

Under Hegel’s leadership, Valgsland joined the Contanan Security Pact in 1946, reinforcing its regional security commitments while charting an independent ideological course within the socialist world. His reforms have transformed symbolic institutions into functional organs of governance, increased public participation in decision-making, and elevated civil liberties and living standards. 

Valgsland is now considered one of the most stable socialist states globally, with no unemployment, a robust social safety net, and a strong civil rights record. It has been designated an “example state” by the Alliance of Nations for its progressive reforms. The country is also a member of OMEC and maintains a permanent seat in the Alliance of Nations, affirming its role as a model for post-revolutionary development.

Wehlen, officially the Republic of Wehlen, is a presidential republic located in Eastern Merkopa. The nation is currently governed by the Wehzek Nationalist Party of Nurist Socialism under the leadership of President Wiktor Smolak. Its capital city is Wraclawitz.

The state of Wehlen was established by Baron Warongrad Reczniek in 1630, who seceded from the Markian Empire to form his own kingdom in a region predominantly inhabited by the Wehzek people. Despite the Wehzek people's longstanding presence in the area, spanning over a thousand years, they had never before managed to unify under a single governmental entity.

Following a bloody revolution in 1914, the monarchical system was dismantled, replaced by a republic. This change heralded a short-lived economic boom, driven by the discovery of gold, diamond mines, and oil in the mountainous areas near Rumburg and Lespia. However, the nation's stability was shattered in 1930 when a civil war erupted following the assassination of the president by a Wehzek royalist. The country was split, with the conflict escalating further in 1930 due to foreign interventions from Arcasia backed the southern factions, while United Contana supported the northern factions. This period also saw armed rebel groups from neighboring Sordland establishing bases within Wehlen.

The civil war, which lasted until 1940, wreaked havoc across Wehlen, leading to widespread starvation, disease, and a massive refugee crisis. Despite the formal end of the conflict in 1940 and the re-establishment of the republic, Arcasian troops were withdrawn in 1936. United Contana then established a peacekeeping brigade in 1937 in Wraclawitz, which remained until 1943. The protracted period of turmoil fueled a strong anti-Arcasian sentiment, which played a significant role in the rise of the Wehzek Nationalist Party of Nurist Socialism. Wiktor Smolak, a pivotal figure during the post-war era, was elected president in 1943, subsequently steering the country towards a one-party state framework.

Despite being rich in natural resources like oil and diamonds, Wehlen is considered to have one of the weakest economies in Eastern Merkopa, exacerbated by its poor record on civil rights and political freedoms. It is often cited as the least favorable nation in Merkopa for starting a business.

Wehlen is a member of the Organization for Merkopan Economic Development (OMEC) and the Alliance of Nations, participating actively in regional economic and political initiatives.

It is the largest military base in Sordland, situated at the heart of Holsord. Camp Strongarm houses three divisions of troops totalling up to fifty thousand soldiers and a military airbase housing a hundred warplanes.

It was created by Colonel Soll after his coup succeeded to exert power in the capital for the longer-term. Currently, it protects the government of Sordland and has the capacity to rapidly redeploy to oppose any real danger a neighbouring country could impose.

The Hill of Pride was named during the declaration of the Kingdom of Sordland, when thousands of countrymen started proudly singing the new anthem of Sordland. It is located at the center of Holsord, in between the most important government structures like the Maroon Palace, The Supreme Court, The Grand National Assembly and the Ministry of Interior.

The Hill of Pride is inside the large capitol park, which gives the Holsordians a chance to relax from the city stress with free time activities in nature. The hill has great symbolic importance because of the declaration of the kingdom and the republic which took place on top of it during the last century.

The Maroon Palace is where the executive branch of the Sordish government is situated. It was constructed to serve as the summer residence of Albrecht Renan, but quickly became a structure of political importance. The turning point was when the Kingdom of Sordland was announced from the balcony of the palace, reflecting the shift of government power from Erlory to Holsord during the transition period.

The Maroon Palace received its name from the maroon painted exterior walls. It has a hundred rooms and several wings housing different branches of executive government. Undearneath the structure is a highly secure situation room where the president is safe from any danger and evaluates any security crisis.

Agnland, a strategic region of Sordland, shares its borders with the region of Nargis and the countries of Agnolia and Rumburg. Its capital city is Arvory, serving a sizeable population of Agno-Sordish, the second largest minority group in the country.

Geographically, Agnland is often seen as an extension of Greater Agnolia, reflecting its historical association with the neighboring country of Agnolia. The regional economy, heavily reliant on trade with Agnolia and the local fishing industry, has historically often struggled with stagnation. Coupled with high unemployment rates, this economic hardship has positioned Agnland as one of the more economically challenged regions in Sordland. Over the years, however, many Agnolian companies that used to operate within the region have relocated, leaving a palpable void in the local economy.

Agnland is bounded by the Eastern Sourne mountains in the north, marking its border with Rumburg. Agnolia lies to its northeast, and the vast Markian Sea flanks the region's eastern edge. The northern landscape is punctuated by hills and mountains, with minimal infrastructure, making traversing the area a challenging task. The region's coastal areas are characterized by bays, fjords, and precipitous cliff lines, underscoring the geographical diversity of Agnland. Agnland also lays claim to Duru Island where former President Tarquin Soll resides.

Bergia, a landlocked region of Sordland, is encircled by the regions of Nargis, Gelsland, and Greater Holsord, and the countries of Wehlen, Lespia, and Rumburg. The capital city, Deyr, is nestled in a river delta area in which many rivers pass and irrigate the farmlands. Bergia is home to a substantial Bludish population, the most significant minority in Sordland.

Sometimes referred to by its old Bludish name 'Bludia,' Bergia covers most of the geographical expanse of Greater Bludia, with the exception of northern territories in Wehlen and Lespia. Despite its thriving economy, the region struggles with high unemployment rates. Agriculture, mining, and steel manufacturing form the bedrock of Bergia's economy, with the Bergia Steel Corporation standing out as a prominent business. The region also houses the Soll Dam, a critical power source for Sordland.

For the followers of the Nurity faith, Bergia is a pilgrimage destination owing to the Archsanctuary of Descension located in Deyr. The region's geography is characterized by mountains on nearly all sides, including the Bergia mountains in the north, the Gumren and Taurus mountains along the western border with Wehlen, and the Maradun mountains towards the south bordering Lespia. 

The fertile river deltas nestled among these mountains are interspersed with cities and farmlands. Bergia also hosts a significant portion of the Maris forest, stretching from Sarna in the north to Gelsord.

Gelsland, bordering the regions of Nargis, Bergia and Greater Holsord, proudly hosts its administrative capital, Gelsord along with the cities of Ribery and Antel.

Gelsland's economy draws on a broad spectrum of industries. Many experimental factories and research and design centres find their home in the region, along with an array of small businesses. Known as Sordland's hub for technology and scientific exploration, Gelsord plays a leading role in shaping the regional identity. The past decade has seen a marked growth in production sectors, particularly those involved with mechanical engineering and the electronics industry. However, the output of these activities are often taken out of the city and to larger havens such as Lachaven or Holsord for business before the local benefit.

From a geographical perspective, Gelsland presents a remarkable array of natural features. The northernmost parts of the Maris forest spread out from Gelsord to Sarna, forming an integral part of the regional ecosystem. The Markian Sea coast on the eastern side of Gelsland carves out a dramatic coastline of bays, cliff lines, and tiny islands. Among these, the renowned Antel Rock and the infamous Antel Rock Prison stand as prominent landmarks.

Greater Holsord, one of the most important regions of Sordland, shares its borders with Gruni, Gelsland, Bergia, and Lorren, as well as the neighboring country of Lespia. The region's governance operates from Holsord, the bustling capital of Sordland, boasting an impressive population density that sets it apart from other Sordish regions.

The economy of Greater Holsord is very robust and old, evident in its diverse industrial landscape. Large-scale businesses find their home in this region, with industries spanning from construction and logistics to mechanical engineering, as well as banking and some tourism. This economic dynamism lends Greater Holsord a competitive edge, setting it in close contest with the region of Nargis.

The geography of Greater Holsord is characterized by the serene flow of the Eskel River, tracing its path through Jen, Holsord, and Conriat. The northern coast of the region, lining the Markian Sea, is distinguished by the famed Conriat Bay, an attraction for locals and tourists alike. Moreover, the historical city of Erlory, the former capital, nestles within this region, adding a layer of historical depth to the modern vitality of Greater Holsord.

Nargis shares its borders with Agnland, Gelsland, Bergia, and Greater Holsord, as well as the neighboring country of Rumburg. Lachaven, known commonly as "The Gateway" is the economic nerve center of Sordland, serves as the regional capital and contributes significantly to the region's population density and economic output.

The economy of Nargis pulses with vitality, largely credited to Lachaven's role as a trade hub. Despite the robust economy, Nargis features expansive tracts of undeveloped land, the largest of such areas across Sordland. The region also boasts significant reserves of oil and other untapped natural resources, thus relying heavily on the oil and natural gas sectors, as well as agriculture and tourism. Gasom Corporation, a key player in the region, bolsters its economic profile with significant operations.

Geographically, Nargis is situated against the Sourne mountains to the north, bordering Rumburg, and the Cavendir mountain to the west. Its western expanse is characterized by hilly terrain interspersed with mountains, posing a significant challenge to infrastructure development and traversal. The region's eastern boundary graces the Markian Sea through the Gulf of Nargis, forming a scenic coastline adorned by bays and cliff lines.

Bergia Steel was founded in 1889 and is the largest fully private corporation among the Big Four, the companies at the center of Sordland's ownership debate. It is the primary steel manufacturer of Sordland and operates mainly in the Bergia region. It also works in steel construction projects and is highly successful due to the experienced architects and engineers they possess.

Bergia Steel has been contracted by Wehlen for several works close to the Sordish border, and this has led many to increase investments and trust due to its potential to rival the state corporations, which mainly dominate the public-sector contracts. Walter Tusk owns a majority stake in the corporation.

Gasom is a privately owned Sordish energy company that mainly extracts natural gas and engineering complex machinery. Currently it is headquartered in Lachaven but it was originally incorporated in Holsord in 1925. Gasom is one of the largest corporations in Sordland. The Revolution’s Energy Department of United Contana had started the company as a joint venture with Sordish businessmen with the ambitions to influence Sordland economically. 

The political instability of the Coup of 27 and the following Sordish Civil War led the Contanan state to sell its shares. This left the board entirely to several Sordish businessmen who acquired the assets for cheap due to the post-civil war recession. 

In 1930 Ewald Alphonso, who had acquired a slim majority of the shares, was elected CEO. Under Alphonso’s tenure, Gasom hired world-class civil, electrical, mechanical, chemical, and petroleum engineers from the Anrakan Archipelago and Merkopa. The company expanded its primary operations around Narbel, in the Nargis region, where many untapped natural gas resources are located. 

The investment led by the corporation and the excavation in and around Narbel turned it from a town to a city, allowing the employment of all sorts for the local populace needing more urban development. The Nature Preservation Foundation criticized the damage to natural wildlife done by the corporation. Still, the corporation has fulfilled most of the gas needs of Sordland, increasing its energy independence and autarky strategy promoted by the Tarquin Soll government.

In 1932, Gasom sold a small part of its shares to the state under the nationalization initiative of Tarquin Soll to fund further operations. It applied for and won the contract award for the co-construction of the Erzaren Soll Dam. The highly talented engineers of Gasom were a vital propellent of the mega-project. 

Besides the state-owned Sordish State Corporation and the Sordish Grid Corporation contributing to the project, Gasom was the only majority privately owned corporation to work on the construction. The corporation grew rapidly and successfully until the mid-1940s and relocated its headquarters to Lachaven.

Ewald Alphonso resigned from his role as CEO and became the board’s chairman due to his pressing political ambitions in 1945. After the change in the leadership to a new CEO, the company has been stagnating and seeking further investment to increase its declining production capacity.

The Heart of Sordland Conglomerate (HOS) is a multi-industry corporation worth tens of billions of SR. Alongside Bergia Steel, it is one of the two privately held corporations among the Big Four. They are involved in many industries, but only have a monopoly in the media industry through the ownership of Sordland Today and the Sordish Broadcasting Corporation. They are heavily involved in radio, television, and advertising sectors. It was founded by Konrath Koronti, the first modern Sordish entrepreneur.

Sordish citizens employed by HOS enjoy many benefits, such as huge salary bonuses, free private healthcare and free housing. In the last decade, a leadership question has engulfed the organization, which slowed down its revenue, but it still remains a behemoth that can influence the economy, as well as the perception of the society on certain issues.

Recently, the eldest son of Konrath,Marcel Koronti has been the rising star of the conglomerate and the potential candidate for CEO.

Founded in 1899, the Sordish Grid Corporation is tasked with constructing and maintaining the energy infrastructure in the country. It is in charge of every government owned energy source and distribution.

It also specializes in their construction, in this field it is more experienced and efficient than other corporations. The fact that it is a government corporation does a cause a lack of competitiveness and oversight, but overall they have a good track record from building power stations to dams to power lines to desolate areas.

Founded in 1891, the Sordish State Corporation (SSC) is the main government corporation tasked with running public construction contracts in Sordland. It is one of the two state-owned enterprises among the Big Four. Widely regarded as the most honorable company in the country, it has a long and solid track record of accomplishing critical projects.

In the recent years, the efficiency of the corporation seems to have dropped due to the recession and the somehow corrupt management structure. It is still considered the safest bet for big projects in the minds of many government officials.

In the political lexicon of Sordland, 'The Old Guard' is a term used to denote a purported group of influential individuals within the government. The nature and influence of this group, however, are subjects of considerable debate and speculation.

The concept of 'The Old Guard' is often associated with theories of a deep state, a hidden network of power said to exert control over the state apparatus. This clandestine web of influence is rumored to permeate key organizations within the government, effectively shaping policy and decision-making from behind the scenes. Critics, however, dismiss such notions as urban myths, challenging the existence of such a widespread and influential entity.

It's widely speculated that 'The Old Guard' took root during the Soll era, functioning as a security mechanism to maintain control and stability within the government. However, the shroud of secrecy remains intact, as there have been no public admissions or definitive evidence to confirm the identities of its alleged members. This enduring ambiguity ensures 'The Old Guard' remains a subject of intrigue, conjecture, and controversy within Sordland's political landscape.

The term "Oligarchs" in the context of Sordland refers to a select group of individuals who, through strategic acquisition of state assets during periods of privatization, have amassed significant wealth and control over extensive industrial networks. These elites, characterized by their economic influence, often emerge from economic liberalization periods, seizing the opportunity to purchase public assets at significantly reduced prices.

Several oligarchs are known to be affiliated with prominent groups such as the Lotherberg Group and the National Business Council, further solidifying their influence in both economic and political spheres. However, their reach extends beyond Sordland's borders, as they frequently engage in foreign direct investments, thereby securing their financial interests on an international scale.

Despite their affluence within Sordland, the oligarchs' precise role and influence within the nation's political and economic framework remain subjects of ongoing debate. Their ability to manipulate economic levers and shape policy decisions shows their substantial sway over the nation's trajectory. Yet, their propensity for foreign investments indicates a broader vision, one that acknowledges the importance of international economic interconnectivity. This duality is at the heart of understanding the role of oligarchs in modern Sordland.

The Reformist Alliance, centered around the People’s Freedom and Justice Party (PFJP), represents a significant faction in the political landscape of Sordland. Historically, this alliance has brought together a variety of political ideologies, from socialists and communists to liberals, who find common ground in their shared aspiration for social and political reform. This faction's existence reflects a broader trend in Sordland's history, highlighting the nation's continual struggle between tradition and progress.

Challenges abound for the Reformist Alliance due to Sordland's electoral system, which critics argue disproportionately benefits established parties.
